title: Accuracy of a Goldreich–Levin stage
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, let $0<\tau\le 1$, and let $E$ assign a rational estimate to each coordinate set $J\subseteq[n]$ and each subset of $J$. Suppose that for every such $J$ and subset $S$, the estimate differs from the restricted Fourier weight of $f$ by less than $\tau^2/4$. For any $k<n$ and any family of subsets of $[n]$, consider the candidates obtained by adjoining or omitting coordinate $k$ from members of that family; for every candidate $S$, the estimate at the prefix of the first $k+1$ coordinates and the free-coordinate part of $S$ differs from the corresponding restricted Fourier weight by less than $\tau^2/4$.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
rational estimate indexed by coordinate sets and their subsets
estimate approximates every restricted Fourier weight within $\tau^2/4$
